## claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929 retires on the Claude API Nov 30, 2026; use claude-sonnet-5-5 [Verified]

Replaced claude-sonnet-4-5 with claude-sonnet-5-5 in all 12 JS files (api/*, demo/server*.js, scripts/*.js, src/rhetorical.js), including the model value stamped into cached entries. Added test/model.test.js, which scans the JS source for the old model ID, thinking-disabled and tool_choice. Left scripts/*-backup.json as historical data. claude-sonnet-4-5(-20250929) retires 2026-11-30; requests with it will fail afterwards.

> | November 30, 2026 | `claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929` | `claude-sonnet-5-5` |

Source: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/model-deprecations.md

### Proof

| Check | Before | After | New failures |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| model-test | fail (1) | pass | 0 |

Where checks ran: Docker container node:22-bookworm; install scripts disabled; no host env or mounts besides the repo copy; no credentials, so no live API calls

### Unproven

- No live call to claude-sonnet-5-5 was made
- Existing cached chunks in backup JSON still say model claude-sonnet-4-5
- SDK left at 0.82.0; not checked against the new model
- No provider validator was run.

### Behaviour changes

- Output tone, length and JSON adherence may differ on Sonnet 5.5; reviewers should spot-check generated scripts
- Confirmed no call sends thinking:{type:'disabled'} or tool_choice (any/tool), which return 400 on Sonnet 5.5; none were found, so nothing changed for that
- Cost and latency may differ

change.title: npm @anthropic-ai/sdk 1.0.0 sends API version 2026-10-21 by default; MessageParam becomes a union, temperature/top_p/top_k removed, Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry SDKs must move to v1 too

source.quote: * **api:** add support for new API version 2026-10-21

tasks.reasoning:
The repo uses @anthropic-ai/sdk 0.82.0 plus many raw HTTP calls that send their own anthropic-version, probably 2023-06-01. Moving to SDK 1.0.0 / API 2026-10-21 means the following, all in one PR:
- Strip temperature/top_p/top_k, which become a 400 error. Whether the code sends them is unknown because request bodies were not fully read; the agent must check.
- Adapt to MessageParam becoming a union.
- Check the document/citation placement rules.
- Decide on OTel spans.
- Bump the header in the HTTP calls.
Old SDKs keep sending 2023-06-01 and no removal date is given, so nothing breaks today. The urgency is low-medium.
This task also resolves these changes. Handle each in the same change, and say in the PR how:
- anthropic:2026-10-21-api-version-2026-10-21 (api-version): New Claude API version 2026-10-21 (anthropic-version header); SDKs older than the new majors keep sending 2023-06-01. SDK 1.0.0 sends anthropic-version 2026-10-21 by default. The same PR should bump the explicit anthropic-version header in the raw HTTP POST /v1/messages calls so the whole repo moves to one API version together.
  Source: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/migration-2026-10-21.md
  "This guide lists the code changes for moving from API version `2023-06-01` to `2026-10-21`."
- anthropic:2026-10-21-sampling-params-removed (field-removed): In API version 2026-10-21, temperature, top_p and top_k in Messages and Batch requests return 400. temperature/top_p/top_k return 400 only under API version 2026-10-21, which this upgrade adopts. The parameters must be stripped from SDK and HTTP request bodies in the same PR.
  Source: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/migration-2026-10-21.md
  "In `2026-10-21`, a request that sends `temperature`, `top_p`, or `top_k` returns a 400 error, even at the parameter’s default value."
- anthropic:2026-10-21-document-citations-user-assistant-errors (other): In API version 2026-10-21, document blocks in assistant messages and citations on text blocks in user messages return 400. This only applies under 2026-10-21. The same PR should confirm no request places document blocks in assistant messages or citations on user text blocks.
  Source: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/migration-2026-10-21.md
  "In `2026-10-21`, a request that places a `document` block directly in an `assistant` message returns a 400 error."
- anthropic:2026-10-14-ts-sdk-otel-default (other): TypeScript SDK 0.134.0 auto-creates OpenTelemetry spans and trace headers if a global tracer provider exists (unsure if affects; opt out with openTelemetry:false). Going from 0.82.0 to 1.0.0 crosses 0.134.0. Check whether the app registers a global OpenTelemetry tracer provider, and pass openTelemetry:false if spans are unwanted.
  Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-typescript/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md
  "If your app registers a global tracer provider, the SDK will create spans with it after upgrading, and they'll be exported with the rest of your traces."

review.summary: The package bump to @anthropic-ai/sdk ^1.0.0 is reasonable. The SDK-based call sites the match agent named (demo/server.js:87, demo/server_old.js:132/203, src/rhetorical.js:49) are not touched or exercised at all. Moving them to 2026-10-21 changes live production behaviour: the request schema, the response shape the code reads via `data.content?.[0]?.text`, and error semantics. Nothing tests this; every call path is a live call. I could not confirm what 2026-10-21 changes in the raw HTTP contract beyond the CHANGELOG quote. Check the API versioning docs before shipping. Keeping 2023-06-01 here would have been the minimal change.
Same unforced header bump in the cache-seeding scripts. Any difference in output under the new version would be written into Upstash as Tier-1 cached scripts, with no test coverage.

These are the actual SDK consumers (lines 87, 132, 203, 49) and the diff does not touch them. Whether they still work on SDK 1.0 is unverified. Open questions: does the import/require style still resolve (e.g. `.default` vs the CommonJS export), do they rely on response fields or MessageParam shapes that changed, and do they use helpers like `stream`/`countTokens` that may have moved? The test only greps them for `temperature:`/`top_p:`/`top_k:` and never loads them.

The test passes against a mocked fetch and a text grep, which is circular: it asserts what the diff wrote rather than application behaviour. The async IIFE has no `.catch`, so a failure relies on Node's unhandled-rejection exit behaviour (Node ≥15) to fail the check. It does not cover any repo call site.

Pre-existing: the file contains unresolved merge-conflict markers (`<<<<<<< HEAD` / `>>>>>>> db8f43e`) and cannot parse. The diff edits this file without noticing, and the test's text grep cannot catch it. This is not caused by the PR, but it shows this endpoint is not being exercised by any check.

SDK 1.0 adds runtime dependencies (`@opentelemetry/api`, `standardwebhooks`) and changes license from MIT to Apache-2.0. Probably fine, but confirm the license is acceptable. Also check SDK 1.0's `engines` field against the Node version on the deployment target (Vercel); I could not confirm it.
